title: feat: merge the Support project into Dev
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Follow-up to #15358. Support becomes a tab inside Dev instead of a separate project, so issues, PRs, quests, app submissions and user reports live in one place.

- Every issue goes to Dev; a new `Source` field (Team / Community) is set from the author, replacing the dev/support project choice
- Community issues keep their High/Low priority (Urgent for paying customers), now on Dev's Priority field
- The classifier no longer picks a project; priority and tracking-issue parents depend on whether the author is on the team

The Support project gets closed (not deleted) after this is merged. Dry run: community issues → `Community` + priority, team/relayed/CI issues → `Team` + tracking parent.

gist.headline: One hive desk
gist.blurb: Support moved its little desk into Dev. Community reports, quests, apps, issues, and PRs now gather under one warm roof, with their source and priority labels intact.
gist.summary: Merged the Support GitHub project into Dev so all issues, PRs, quests, app submissions, and user reports use Dev’s new Team/Community Source field and shared Priority field, while team-authored items retain tracking-issue parents.
gist.impact: Maintainers can triage community work and team work from one Dev project, with community High/Low (and paying-customer Urgent) priorities preserved and team or CI work still linked to its tracking parent.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the Support desk being gently moved into a larger Dev garden workshop: labeled Team and Community inbox trays feed one shared issue board, while a Priority flowerbed keeps High, Low, and Urgent blooms organized. Polli should actively carry a tiny Support sign into the cozy workspace, signaling consolidation rather than removal; the monitor robot can happily sort issue cards.
